verification.reasoning: The first year is the wage he already has, before any raise has been applied.
One year of 2.5% growth applied to $32,000, which is the wage he is giving up in the second study year.
Two years of compounding: the second raise is applied to $32,800, not to the original $32,000.
Three years of compounding on $32,000. Compounding is why the forgone amount is larger than four times the starting wage.
Tuition of $12,750 charged in each of the 4 study years.
The economic cost is the cash paid out plus the income never received: $132,880.50 forgone plus $51,000.00 of tuition.
$183,880.50 divided by the $19,400 annual advantage. Recovery is measured against the true cost, not against tuition alone.
$132,880.50 of forgone earnings against $51,000.00 of tuition — the invisible half of the cost is more than twice the half that arrives as a bill.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: No assumption is named.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named and its effect on the conclusion is stated.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named, tested against the scenario, and bounded.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The conclusion is stated as certain when the scenario does not support that.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known and how it limits the conclusion.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known, how it limits the conclusion, and what would resolve it.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The error is not located.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The response says the work is wrong but not where or why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response locates the first wrong step and states the misconception behind it.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response locates the error, names the misconception, and gives a check that would have caught it.

judgment.prompt: A friend tells Marcus the programme "costs $51,000". Explain what that figure leaves out, why the omitted part is easy to miss, and what it does to the recovery period.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Identifies the $132,880.50 of forgone earnings as the omission, and explains that it never appears as a bill because it is income that simply never arrives.
States that counting tuition alone would give a recovery period of about 2.6 years against the 9.5 years the full cost produces.
Explains that the forgone side compounds, so it grows with the length of the programme rather than staying fixed.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the $51,000.00 tuition figure and the $132,880.50 forgone-earnings figure side by side.
lookFors: The response explains why an opportunity cost is invisible, not merely that it was forgotten.
The response connects the omission to a specific consequence for the recovery period.
A response that computes the tuition-only recovery period itself is stronger than one that only says it would be shorter.
judgment.commonMisconception: Treating the cost of a programme as the amount that appears on the invoice.

judgment.prompt: The model gives Marcus a raise of 2.5% in each year he is not studying. Say what would happen to the true cost if that raise pattern were smaller, and name one thing about his job that would make the 2.5% assumption unsafe.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: States that a smaller raise pattern lowers the forgone earnings, lowering the true cost below $183,880.50 and shortening the 9.5-year recovery.
Names a specific reason the assumption could fail, such as raises being tied to a role he would leave anyway, or the wage in that job having a ceiling.
evidenceRequirements: Refers to the compounded fourth-year figure of $34,460.50 or to the $132,880.50 total when describing what the raise assumption controls.
lookFors: The response identifies the raise pattern as an assumption about the alternative, not about the programme.
The response gives a mechanism for the assumption failing rather than saying only that it "might not happen".

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
oracle.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic over BigInt; no binary floating point
oracle.limits: Recomputation establishes that the key follows from the stated figures. It does not by itself establish that the model chosen is the right model for the scenario; that is carried by the per-item reasoning, the parameter-visibility check, and human review.
